title: Haunted Alabama: Montevallo's Palmer Hall and its popular poltergeist
excerpt: Palmer Hall at the University of Montevallo is home to stories of a ghost named "Trummie," with mysterious occurrences becoming a beloved campus tradition.
content:
Haunted Alabama: Montevallo's Palmer Hall and its popular poltergeist

MONTEVALLO, Ala. —

Palmer Hall at the University of Montevallo has long been the stage for performances, but tales of a ghost named "Trummie" have made it a source of intrigue and campus tradition.

Flickering lights, loud banging and doors that open on their own are among the mysterious happenings attributed to Walter Trumbauer, affectionately known as Trummie.

"Palmer Hall was originally built in 1929. Walter Trumbauer had traveled to Europe looking at different theaters that he thought he might want to reconstruct here. He found one in Germany called the Volksbühne. He came back here and started to work with architects to redesign it. So this is an exact replica of that theater," said Andrew Fancher, director of operations at Palmer Auditorium.

Fancher, whose father and grandfather worked on campus, grew up hearing stories of Trummie. After spending 20 years working in the theater, he now has his own experiences to share.

"There are a lot of various things that have happened for me over the times here. A lot of it comes on late nights here on College Night. Working on stage you might see a light spark flashing on the electric system above us without any power to it. Probably our most vivid thing is it almost looks like it can take a long exposure of a car light. This light that's in between all of us and kind of left this light streak behind," Fancher said.

He added that Trummie is most active at the beginning of the year as students prepare for College Night, an annual tradition where they choose sides based on the university's colors.

"Sometimes confetti will fall from the ceiling. So we have these cut lights out here in the ceiling. Sometimes things will fall through there. We've even gotten notes on letterhead that was from the 30s and 40s that fall out of there during college night."

Fancher said he has never doubted the presence of a poltergeist, noting that his years in the building have solidified his belief.

"I did have a belief of it before I got here, but, you work in this building for 20 years, and you definitely have to have something to explain the unexplainable," he said.

One of the most famous stories tied to Trummie involves the lights and scenery above the stage.

"I think the most famous thing from Trumbauer for me is that he was swinging the battens, which are what scenery and lights are hanging on to above us, to whichever side he thinks is going to win college night. Now, I've only seen this one time, in my 20 years. But a lot of people have similar experiences of catching it. Once or twice, seeing the batten swinging, it doesn't just swing freely. It swings to one side and comes back and stops," Fancher said.

Despite Trummie's mischievous nature, Fancher said the ghost is generally friendly, and there are no plans to rid Palmer Hall of its spectral resident.

"Trummie is mischievous at times, but generally always friendly," Fancher said.
